prompt:
Select the Pen tool (P) and draw a straight two-point line, clicking at roughly (200,300) and (500,300). Do NOT press Enter (Enter is "Done" and ends the vector edit session). Instead press Escape once — this switches the pen from chain-extending mode into node/path edit while keeping you inside the same vector edit session. Then click directly on the middle of the existing segment at about (350,300) to insert one extra anchor point onto the path (a single continuous vertex on the same path, not a new path). Do not open the pen tool dropdown while a draw is active.

Base your verdict only on the final result: approve if the line ends with three anchors on one continuous path (both original endpoints plus the inserted middle vertex). Exploration detours or minor UI friction you recovered from are not blockers.

At the very end of your final message, state whether the task went smoothly. If everything worked without problems, end with exactly "verdict: approve". If you hit any problems, bugs, or blockers, briefly say what went wrong and end with exactly "verdict: not-approve".

With the Pen tool (P), draw a V (three clicks: (200,250), (260,350), (320,250)). Do NOT press Enter (Enter is "Done" and exits the vector edit session); instead press Escape once to end the current chain while staying inside the same vector edit session. Still in that session with the pen, draw one more separate short two-point stroke nearby (e.g. (380,250) to (440,300)), then press Escape again to end that chain and exit the session. Final state: both strokes exist as subpaths of a single vector, created within one edit session.

At the very end of your final message, state whether the task went smoothly. If everything worked without problems, end with exactly "verdict: approve". If you hit any problems, bugs, or blockers, briefly say what went wrong and end with exactly "verdict: not-approve".

Draw three overlapping squares in this exact order: a 100x100 first, then a 150x150, then a 200x200, each partly covering the previous one. Select the first (smallest) square and step it exactly one layer up with Ctrl+Alt+ArrowUp (on this Linux environment the command modifier is Ctrl, not Cmd), so it sits above the 150px square but still below the 200px one. Leave the "Use arrows to rotate layers" preference at its default (OFF) so the arrow shortcut reorders layers instead of rotating.

At the very end of your final message, state whether the task went smoothly. If everything worked without problems, end with exactly "verdict: approve". If you hit any problems, bugs, or blockers, briefly say what went wrong and end with exactly "verdict: not-approve".

Create a text layer with the text "Chapter One". In this app small caps is set via the Case control in the Type settings (a text-case value), not a Details-tab OpenType toggle. The default Inter (upright) does not support small caps, so first switch the layer to a font that does — e.g. Roboto or Montserrat. Then set the Case control to Small caps.

At the very end of your final message, state whether the task went smoothly. If everything worked without problems, end with exactly "verdict: approve". If you hit any problems, bugs, or blockers, briefly say what went wrong and end with exactly "verdict: not-approve".

Create a text layer with the text "Display size" and set its font to Roboto Flex (the bundled variable font that has an optical size (opsz) axis; the default Inter does not). Open the Type settings popover via the sliders button in the Typography section, switch to the Variable tab, and turn OFF the automatic optical size toggle so the opsz axis stops tracking the font size.

At the very end of your final message, state whether the task went smoothly. If everything worked without problems, end with exactly "verdict: approve". If you hit any problems, bugs, or blockers, briefly say what went wrong and end with exactly "verdict: not-approve".

Create a text layer with the text "Fine tune" and set its font to Roboto Flex (the bundled variable font that exposes an optical size (opsz) axis; the default Inter does not). Open the Type settings popover via the sliders button in the Typography section, switch to the Variable tab, turn OFF the automatic optical size toggle so the manual optical size (opsz) slider appears, then take manual control of the opsz axis and set it to 14.

At the very end of your final message, state whether the task went smoothly. If everything worked without problems, end with exactly "verdict: approve". If you hit any problems, bugs, or blockers, briefly say what went wrong and end with exactly "verdict: not-approve".
